seoTitle: How to Accept Multiple Payment Methods in Jotform
metaDescription: Learn how to combine credit card, PayPal, and other payment gateways on one Jotform in 2026 using conditional logic and embedded payment sub-forms.
intro: A single Jotform form can only connect to one direct payment gateway at a time, so offering multiple payment options requires a workaround using conditional logic and embedded sub-forms. This guide covers building separate payment sub-forms, linking them to a master form with a selection button, and testing the full checkout flow.

steps.heading: Build individual payment sub-forms
steps.body: Create separate standalone forms, each connected to a distinct payment gateway such as Stripe or PayPal.

steps.heading: Build the master form
steps.body: Create your main form layout with contact fields and a single choice radio button for selecting the payment method.

steps.heading: Add the iFrame Embed widget
steps.body: Open the Widgets panel and drag in the iFrame Embed tool to hold each payment sub-form.

steps.heading: Set up conditional logic
steps.body: Configure show and hide rules so the correct payment sub-form iFrame appears based on the radio button selection.

steps.heading: Test the full checkout flow
steps.body: Paste the sub-form URLs into the iFrame containers, adjust frame dimensions, and test the entire multi-payment pipeline in sandbox mode.

faq.question: Why can't I just add two payment gateways to one Jotform form?
faq.answer: Jotform only allows a single direct payment gateway connection per form, which is why the sub-form and conditional logic workaround is needed for multiple options.

faq.question: Does the customer see all payment options at once?
faq.answer: No, conditional logic reveals only the relevant payment sub-form iFrame based on which method the customer selects with the radio button.

faq.question: Can I test this setup before accepting real payments?
faq.answer: Yes, testing the consolidated checkout workflow in sandbox mode is recommended before going live.

faq.question: Will this approach work for both product sales and donations?
faq.answer: Yes, the sub-form and conditional logic method can support various payment types, including product sales and flexible donation amounts.
